bull_case: Data-center/technology MEP demand, modular construction, electrical expansion and disciplined acquisitions sustain high-teens owner-FCF/share growth longer than the market expects.
bear_case: Data-center construction normalizes, working-capital advances reverse, backlog growth slows and the premium multiple compresses toward a mature construction-services profile.
thesis: Reconstructed TTM owner FCF is about $2159.8M or $61.26/share, but current cash generation is unusually aided by advance billings and AP timing. The locked DCF therefore starts Base below TTM cash generation and yields Bear/Base/Bull values of $722.18/$1908.32/$3149.52 versus $1651.37. Price/Base is 0.865x, indicating a meaningful but not extreme expectation gap.

evidence.claim: Reconstructed TTM owner FCF through Q2 2026 is about $2159.8M or $61.26/share before working-capital normalization.
H1 2026 OCF was $1.528B versus $164.5M in H1 2025, with about $684.7M benefit from billings/deferred revenue and $535.6M from AP/other current liabilities.
Q2 2026 revenue was $3.266B, up 50.3% YoY, and H1 revenue was $6.131B, up 53.1%, including 47.3% same-store H1 growth.
Backlog was $14.06B at June 30, 2026, up 73.1% YoY; technology/data-center projects were the primary driver of same-store backlog growth.
At Q2 2026, cash plus Treasury bills were about $1.906B versus only $54.1M funded debt; lease liabilities were $274.0M.
Locked Bear/Base/Bull values are $722.18/$1908.32/$3149.52; Base terminal fraction is 68.0%.
evidence.source: Deterministic harness valuation from frozen FIX inputs

counterevidence: H1 2026 FCF is materially boosted by project billing and payable timing and should not be treated as a steady-state margin.
Technology customers were already 45% of FY2025 revenue, creating exposure to data-center construction cycles.
Backlog is mostly 6-12 month visibility and is cancellable; it is not a 5-10 year contract base.
Acquisitions contribute to growth and can reduce comparability across periods.
unknowns: Normalized owner FCF after advance-payment timing reverses.
Durable technology/data-center revenue share after the current buildout cycle.
Long-run modular capacity returns on 2026 building purchases.
falsifiers: Backlog decelerates sharply while advance billings reverse and same-store growth falls below Base assumptions.
Technology/data-center project cancellations materially impair gross margin or working capital.
Normalized FCF/share fails to grow after current advance-payment benefits wash out.
